name: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Sallām al-Jumaḥī al-Baṣrī
summary: Basran man of letters, pupil of Ḥammād ibn Salama, author of Ṭabaqāt fuḥūl al-shuʿarāʾ, the first book to sort the poets into classes; Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Thaʿlab transmitted from him.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī counts Muḥammad ibn Sallām among the men of letters and names his book on the classes of the poets (Ṭabaqāt al-shuʿarāʾ). He learned from Ḥammād ibn Salama, and the imam Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Thaʿlab transmitted from him.
Al-Zubaydī counts him in the fifth generation of the lexicographers of Basra. He died in Baghdad in 232/847.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 216–218
İbn Sellâm el-Cumahî, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
